newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat-Spring wheat bids inch up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat-Spring wheat bids inch up.

text.p: Bids for dark northern spring wheat were higher Wednesday in line with gains on the Minneapolis Grain Exchange, cash dealers said.
"It's really quiet," said a Montana dealer. "Farmers don't like these prices."
MGE September wheat settled up two cents per bushel, and other months were 5-1/2 to one cent per bushel higher.
Rallies in futures and cash markets will continue to be capped by the prospect for a bountiful spring wheat crop.
"The spring wheat is looking absolutely excellent," said a Montana dealer.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture will issue spring wheat acreage forecasts on Monday. Analysts expect spring wheat acreage to range from 17.6 to 20.0 million acres and durum wheat acreage to range from 2.9 to 3.6 million acres.
White wheat bids were under pressure from expectations that the impending Pakistani wheat tender will not be a white wheat sale, dealers said. The tender result was still awaited.
